solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Force small lock

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone forcing a little padlock open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door or padlock, but here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is pressure or emphasis exerted on something, a synonym of force as a noun.

clue.text: Watch copper full of energy in predicament

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside, so the next word sits within the one before

parts.note: to be in a state is to be in a predicament

indicators.note: being in something means lying inside it, so the policeman group goes inside the predicament word

parts.note: PC, police constable, is a copper
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A policeman, full of beans, gets himself into a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two insertions: energy first goes inside the copper, and that pair then goes into the predicament word just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to look on as an onlooker at an event, so it is to watch.

clue.text: Clark Kent, say, on the subject of booze

parts.note: RE means regarding or concerning
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Superman's alter ego is asked about his drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Kent works as a newspaper journalist at the Daily Planet, an example of the job; 'say' flags him as one instance.

clue.text: What you get your teeth into is near for a change

definitions.text: What you get your teeth into

indicators.note: making a change to the preceding letters means rearranging them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cosy line about something you sink your teeth into being close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A sarnie is British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: You bite into a sandwich, so the playful definition describes the snack by what you do with it.

clue.text: Laid on quiet Roman poet to get into rose

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so the poet sits within the colour word

parts.note: rose is a shade of red
Ovid wrote the Metamorphoses

explanation.surface: A gardener's instruction for a Latin poet to climb into a rose bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' reads as the flower or the past tense of rise; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid on, such as food or transport, has been supplied or arranged, which is what provided means.

clue.text: Run away

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase, a running away

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
someone away is out

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a rout is a disorderly flight, a running away.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing defeat in which the losing side flees in disorder.

clue.text: Perhaps, an inhabitant of Greenwich's mostly foul drink

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: vile means foul or disgusting
lager is a drink

explanation.surface: A complaint about the dreadful beer served in Greenwich.
explanation.walkthrough: Greenwich here is Greenwich Village in New York, not the London borough; 'Perhaps' signals it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in Greenwich Village is a villager, an example of a village resident.

clue.text: Unimportant item is possibly cut short

explanation.surface: A trivial point that might be trimmed from a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as DE-TAIL, taking off the end, which is what cutting short does.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a small, minor particular, so an unimportant item; split in two, it means docking a tail.

clue.text: Democrat antagonism results in liability

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat
anger is hostile feeling, antagonism

explanation.surface: A political comment that partisan hostility becomes a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A liability can be a hazard or risk, something that exposes you to harm, close to danger.

clue.text: Virtuoso is to apply much force around pawn

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the force word wraps the chess piece

parts.note: to exert is to apply force
P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: A chess virtuoso pushing hard with a pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is someone highly skilled in an art, a synonym of an expert.

clue.text: Popular on the back of round report

parts.note: a round of ammunition is a bullet
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Something becoming popular after a round of reporting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the back of' puts the first word after the round; 'report' also nods at the noise of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news statement, a kind of report.

clue.text: Dish and excellent book on it

parts.note: rare can mean unusually good
B is the abbreviation for book
taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine book and a tasty dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese melted on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit is a savoury preparation of seasoned melted cheese on toast, a dish.

clue.text: Tramline starts here?

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sign at the start of a tram route.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue word rearranges to the answer, and a tram line does begin at a terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal is the end station of a transport route, where a line begins or ends.

clue.text: Sensitive about morning hunger

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the sensitive word wraps the time of day

parts.note: fine means delicate or sensitive
a.m. denotes morning

explanation.surface: Someone touchy about feeling peckish first thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A famine is extreme scarcity of food, widespread hunger.

clue.text: Relative trouble admitting what's at the heart of hearing

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the trouble word takes something inside

parts.note: bother means trouble

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, so only the middle of the next word is kept

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters in hearing

explanation.surface: A family member having difficulty with their ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother is a male sibling, one kind of relative.

clue.text: Perhaps elder Romeo wrapped by sort of shirt

indicators.note: being wrapped by something means being enclosed in it, so the letter goes inside the shirt word

parts.note: a tee is a T-shirt
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An older Romeo dressed in a T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elder' looks like an older person, but it is the elder tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a shrub or small tree with white flowers, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Erudite poet, Edward

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse
Ned is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A name check for the poet Edward Lear as a scholarly man.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear was the poet, so the surface is literally true, but Edward is used separately as NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned describes someone with much scholarly knowledge, a synonym of erudite.

clue.text: Happily pleased to accept onset of terrific support

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the jumble holds the kept letter
happily suggests a carefree jumble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so just the first letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of terrific

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully agreeing to take on wonderful backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is a base on which a statue or column stands, so a support.

clue.text: Bliss is being in show

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so the short word goes within the show

parts.note: to parade is to show off, and a parade is a display
taken as written

explanation.surface: The thrill of performing in a show is sheer bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a state of perfect happiness, a synonym of bliss.

clue.text: Stupid — unlike any entries here

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: every answer in this crossword has a clue

explanation.walkthrough: The second half refers to the crossword itself: each grid entry comes with a clue, so being without one makes it unlike them.
explanation.definitionFit: Clueless is informal for ignorant or dense, and literally means having no clue.

clue.text: I have turned into one who's taken out stray

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so the turned letters sit inside the companion word

parts.note: a date is the person you take out romantically

indicators.note: turned means turned around, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone confessing they have gone off with a person who was eliminated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken out' could mean killed or removed; here it is someone taken out on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate is to stray from a set course or standard.

clue.text: Clog dance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to gather into a lump and choke up, as snow does on a horse's hoof
second meaning: a formal social dance

explanation.walkthrough: Together the words suggest clog dancing in wooden shoes; separately one is a verb for choking up with lumps and the other a formal party.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to form lumps that obstruct; as a noun it is a grand social gathering for dancing.

clue.text: A car with no-good sorts

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
a heel is a contemptible, untrustworthy person

explanation.surface: A vehicle full of shady characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheels is informal slang for a person's car, so the plural form stands for a single vehicle.

clue.text: Pressure missing from story of an option for farmers

indicators.note: missing from means absent from, so a letter is taken out of the following word

parts.note: a parable is a moral story
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A tale for farmers that lacks tension.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable describes land used for growing crops, one of the uses a farmer may choose for fields.

clue.text: Servant carrying round starter of tomato soup

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it, so the servant word encloses the others

parts.note: a page is a young servant or attendant
O is round in shape

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of tomato

explanation.surface: A waiter bringing out a first course of tomato soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a menu course, which suits the soup, but it only takes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick soup, from the French word for soup.

clue.text: Hard other ranks snare a pest?

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks
to net is to snare or catch

explanation.surface: Tough soldiers trying to trap a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornet is a large stinging wasp, one example of a pest, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Last month to make a speech for paper, say

parts.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December
to orate is to deliver a speech

explanation.surface: A columnist recalling a talk given last month for the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like a newspaper, but it is the verb, to hang wallpaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Papering a room is one way to decorate it, so the verb is an example of decorating.

clue.text: Great, mature maiden turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read upward, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to age is to mature
M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An older single woman arriving is greeted as wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for great or excellent, from the Greek for large.

clue.text: Dash ahead of beer to rankle

parts.note: an em dash is a long dash in printing
bitter is a British pale ale

explanation.surface: Someone rushing for a pint, feeling resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead of' places the first piece before the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter is to make someone resentful, and rankle can likewise mean to cause lasting resentment.

clue.text: Simple account held in queue

indicators.note: being held in something means being enclosed by it, so the short word sits inside the line word

parts.note: a file is a line of people one behind another
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A straightforward bank account kept waiting in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile means easily achieved or superficially simple.

clue.text: A very large number get rid of weight

parts.note: to shed is to get rid of
a load is a weight carried

explanation.surface: Advice to lose a great many pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Shedload is British slang for a large amount or quantity.

clue.text: Those needling fortune-tellers about wife

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the prophets wrap the spouse letter

parts.note: seers foretell the future
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: People pestering clairvoyants about a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needling' reads as annoying; here it means working with a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewers are people who stitch with a needle and thread, so those needling literally.
